    "text": "- Topic Names and Topic Filters are UTF-8 encoded strings, they MUST NOT\nencode to more than 65535 bytes [MQTT-4.7.3-3] . See Section 1.5.3\n\nThere is no limit to the number of levels in a Topic Name or Topic\nFilter, other than that imposed by the overall length of a UTF-8 encoded\nstring.\n\nWhen it performs subscription matching the Server MUST NOT perform any\nnormalization of Topic Names or Topic Filters, or any modification or\nsubstitution of unrecognized characters [MQTT-4.7.3-4] . Each\nnon-wildcarded level in the Topic Filter has to match the corresponding\nlevel in the Topic Name character for character for the match to\nsucceed.\n\nNon normative comment\n\nThe UTF-8 encoding rules mean that the comparison of Topic Filter and\nTopic Name could be performed either by comparing the encoded UTF-8\nbytes, or by comparing decoded Unicode characters\n\nNon normative comment\n\n· “ACCOUNTS” and “Accounts” are two different topic names\n\n· “Accounts payable” is a valid topic name\n\n· “/finance” is different from “finance”\n\nAn Application Message is sent to each Client Subscription whose Topic\nFilter matches the Topic Name attached to an Application Message. The\ntopic resource MAY be either predefined in the Server by an\nadministrator or it MAY be dynamically created by the Server when it\nreceives the first subscription or an Application Message with that\nTopic Name. The Server MAY also use a security component to selectively\nauthorize actions on the topic resource for a given Client.\n\n4.8 Handling errors\n\nUnless stated otherwise, if either the Server or Client encounters a\nprotocol violation, it MUST close the Network Connection on which it\nreceived that Control Packet which caused the protocol violation\n[MQTT-4.8.0-1] ."

    "text": "The payload of a SUBSCRIBE Packet contains a list of Topic Filters\nindicating the Topics to which the Client wants to subscribe. The Topic\nFilters in a SUBSCRIBE packet payload MUST be UTF-8 encoded strings as\ndefined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.8.3-1] . A Server SHOULD support Topic\nfilters that contain the wildcard characters defined in Section 4.7.1 .\nIf it chooses not to support topic filters that contain wildcard\ncharacters it MUST reject any Subscription request whose filter contains\nthem [MQTT-3.8.3-2] . Each filter is followed by a byte called the\nRequested QoS. This gives the maximum QoS level at which the Server can\nsend Application Messages to the Client.\n\nThe payload of a SUBSCRIBE packet MUST contain at least one Topic Filter\n/ QoS pair. A SUBSCRIBE packet with no payload is a protocol violation\n[MQTT-3.8.3-3] . See section 4.8 for information about handling errors.\n\nThe requested maximum QoS field is encoded in the byte following each\nUTF-8 encoded topic name, and these Topic Filter / QoS pairs are packed\ncontiguously.\n\nFigure 3.22 – SUBSCRIBE Packet payload format\n\nDescription\n\n7\n\n6\n\n5\n\n4\n\n3\n\n2\n\n1\n\n0\n\nTopic Filter\n\nbyte 1\n\nLength MSB\n\nbyte 2\n\nLength LSB\n\nbytes 3..N\n\nTopic Filter\n\nRequested QoS\n\nReserved\n\nQoS\n\nbyte N+1\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\nX\n\nX\n\nThe upper 6 bits of the Requested QoS byte are not used in the current\nversion of the protocol. They are reserved for future use. The Server\nMUST treat a SUBSCRIBE packet as malformed and close the Network\nConnection if any of Reserved bits in the payload are non-zero, or QoS\nis not 0,1 or 2 [MQTT-3-8.3-4] .\n\n3.8.3.1 Payload non normative example\n\nFigure 3.23 - Payload byte format non normative example shows the\npayload for the SUBSCRIBE Packet briefly described in Table 3.5 -\nPayload non normative example ."

    "text": "Where the Topic Filter is not identical to any existing Subscription’s\nfilter, a new Subscription is created and all matching retained messages\nare sent.\n\nIf a Server receives a SUBSCRIBE packet that contains multiple Topic\nFilters it MUST handle that packet as if it had received a sequence of\nmultiple SUBSCRIBE packets, except that it combines their responses into\na single SUBACK response [MQTT-3.8.4-4] .\n\nThe SUBACK Packet sent by the Server to the Client MUST contain a return\ncode for each Topic Filter/QoS pair. This return code MUST either show\nthe maximum QoS that was granted for that Subscription or indicate that\nthe subscription failed [ MQTT-3 .8.4-5] . The Server might grant a\nlower maximum QoS than the subscriber requested. The QoS of Payload\nMessages sent in response to a Subscription MUST be the minimum of the\nQoS of the originally published message and the maximum QoS granted by\nthe Server. The server is permitted to send duplicate copies of a\nmessage to a subscriber in the case where the original message was\npublished with QoS 1 and the maximum QoS granted was QoS 0 [ MQTT-3\n.8.4-6] .\n\nNon normative examples If a subscribing Client has been granted maximum\nQoS 1 for a particular Topic Filter, then a QoS 0 Application Message\nmatching the filter is delivered to the Client at QoS 0. This means that\nat most one copy of the message is received by the Client. On the other\nhand a QoS 2 Message published to the same topic is downgraded by the\nServer to QoS 1 for delivery to the Client, so that Client might receive\nduplicate copies of the Message."

It SHOULD\nstore the new QoS 0 message as the new retained message for that topic,\nbut MAY choose to discard it at any time - if this happens there will be\nno retained message for that topic.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-8]\n\nWhen sending a PUBLISH Packet to a Client the Server MUST set the RETAIN\nflag to 1 if a message is sent as a result of a new subscription being\nmade by a Client.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-9]\n\nIt MUST set the RETAIN flag to 0 when a PUBLISH Packet is sent to a\nClient because it matches an established subscription regardless of how\nthe flag was set in the message it received.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-10]\n\nA PUBLISH Packet with a RETAIN flag set to 1 and a payload containing\nzero bytes will be processed as normal by the Server and sent to Clients\nwith a subscription matching the topic name. Additionally any existing\nretained message with the same topic name MUST be removed and any future\nsubscribers for the topic will not receive a retained message.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-11]\n\nA zero byte retained message MUST NOT be stored as a retained message on\nthe Server.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.1-12]\n\nIf the RETAIN flag is 0, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a\nServer, the Server MUST NOT store the message and MUST NOT remove or\nreplace any existing retained message.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.2-1]"
